findings.claim: ScenesSectionPresenter.tsx adds `{" "}` text nodes around the header's bare-count span. This edit falls outside both the Presenter touch point ("the switch row, and the track length taken from the candidate list") and the switch feature itself.
findings.impact: The header button's accessible name changes for every video, whether or not it has change frames. Before the change it read e.g. "Scenes15"; now it reads "Scenes 15". Nothing changes visually, because whitespace-only flex items are not rendered. Existing selectors match `/^Scenes/` or use Playwright's substring match on "Scenes", so no current test breaks. Still, a section without the switch also changes, which the spec's claim that the default mode is identical to today does not record.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/frontend/ScenesSection/ScenesSectionPresenter.tsx:228-231 adds `{" "}` after the title span and after the count span. The only reader that depends on it is the new test ScenesSectionChangePoints.test.tsx:237/242-243. That test matches `/\b15\b/` against header().textContent, and without the space there is no word boundary between "Scenes" and "15". The touch-point list in docs/specs/scenes-change-points.md names the Presenter only for the switch row and the track length.
findings.repro: Mutation: remove the two `{" "}` nodes. Then ScenesSectionChangePoints I5 fails, because textContent "Scenes15…" has no \b before 15. Every other selector found (`/^Scenes/`, Playwright `name: "Scenes"` substring) still matches. Not run; the result comes from reading the code.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariants file exists. This is an unplanned edit to a listed file that changes the accessible name of an unrelated element. It reads as scope creep, not a broken contract.

findings.proposed_fix: Name the header's accessible-name spacing in the Presenter touch point. Alternatively, make the I5 test read the count span directly so the header text does not need to change.

specification_compliance: Every product and test file in the diff appears in the spec's touch-point list: schemas.py, routers/files.py, api.ts, ScenesSectionContainer/Presenter, scenesModel.ts, both locale files, the __tests__ directory, the tests/ directory, all three e2e fixtures, the cases file, both e2e specs, docs/addons/intelligence.md, docs/user-guide/video.md, INDEX.md and the gitlink.
The route reads `clip_change` rows with both the type and the `vec_clip_change` filter, ascending by timestamp_start, and leaves the `timestamps` query unchanged (files.py:1347-1384).

The Presenter touch point says it takes "the track length from the candidate list". That logic actually lives in scenesModel.trackLength and in the Container (Container.tsx:202), and the Presenter only receives `length`. This prose mismatch would not lead to a wrong code change.

Code the change reaches but does not edit and the touch list does not name: hooks/useSceneRows.ts (it absorbs the switch row through lastPart.bottom; spec §7 discusses this), hooks/useWindowPictures.ts (it now receives change times; spec §4 discusses this), and the Ruler component inside the Presenter file (it now draws ticks from `frames`). None of these needed an edit.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The header's accessible name gains spaces between title, count and scene count on every video (Presenter.tsx:228-231). The spec does not describe this.

The `.loft` mount path (Container.tsx:242) sets `changes` but never resets `frameMode` when the answer has no changes. Mode is reset on file change, and a `.loft` never re-fetches on expand, so this is not reachable today.
regression_risks: The default mode passes `frames === candidates`, so the grid, window, dots and keys use the same list as before. While a native request is in flight, `frames` is NO_FRAMES, matching the old `rows ?? []`.
The ResizeObserver in useSceneRows does not observe the switch row. When the switch appears or disappears, the change in root size still triggers a re-measure because the root is observed.
test_coverage: Python: I6 covers ordering (rows inserted in reverse), filtering by both type and table with decoys, an empty list, other files, and a file with changes but no candidates.

Vitest: covers switch visibility for zero, absent and one change; counts; windowing; browse-point retention; no extra requests; the settle delay; L in both modes; dots; keyboard; the collapse/host reopen paths; file change; and the .loft scene-tile route.
e2e: the 384 mouse and 390 touch cases check placement, chip look, height and aria-valuemax invariance, and ruler tick difference.
